text:
alex: FYI customer AcmeCorp reporting auth failures since ~08:02 UTC. They hit our API with JWTs and we return 401/invalid_signature for ~30% of requests. They say it started after their IdP rotated keys.

alex: root error from our logs:
```
AuthService: verify_jwt failed: signature verification failed (kid=abc123) token=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImFiYzEyMyJ9...
Stack: /srv/auth/verify.go:88 verifyKey -> fetchJWKs -> use cached jwk
```

marie: do we see `kid` present in token and also in our JWKS cache? logs show `kid=abc123` but our cached JWKS maybe still old.

sam: timeline pls — did Acme recently switch IdP or rotate?

alex: they confirmed a key rotation at 07:55 UTC and issuing new tokens with new kid; our JWKS fetcher has a 15m TTL and only polls /jwks every 15m, so possible window where token uses new kid but we still only have old keys.

kai: that's a classic kid-not-found / invalid signature window. but we should also be robust: when signature fails, we should force a JWKS refresh and retry verification once.

marie: check whether their JWKS endpoint sent cache headers (cache-control/etag). if the endpoint tells no-cache we should obey.

alex: grabbing HTTP trace from our side when we tried to refresh (08:04):
```
GET https://acme-idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json
200 OK
cache-control: max-age=900
etag: "v1"
body: { "keys": [ { "kid": "oldkid", ... } ] }
```

alex: so they had cache-control 900s, but also rotated keys early — not ideal on their end but we need better handling.

sam: also see customers hitting signature errors with "token expired" and "iat in future" — clock skew too. acme's tokens have iat slightly ahead of our server time by 90s.

kai: set tolerant leeway on JWT validation (e.g., 2-3 minutes) is reasonable. currently we use 30s.

marie: suggest immediate mitigations:
- add retry on signature failure that triggers JWKS refetch (force no-cache) and re-verify once.
- increase default clock skew leeway to 120s but make configurable per-tenant.
- for tokens with kid missing in cache, call JWKS endpoint immediately instead of rejecting.

alex: agree. sample pseudo-fix (for review):
```
func VerifyJWT(token string) error {
  err := verifyWithCachedKeys(token)
  if err == ErrSignatureInvalid || err == ErrKidNotFound {
     refreshJWKs(noCache=true)
     return verifyWithCachedKeys(token)
  }
  return err
}
```

sam: we also need to guard against DoS: don't let malicious clients force our service to hammer their IdP. add rate-limit per-tenant on forced JWKS refresh (e.g., once per 30s) and exponential backoff.

kai: Also log when we do forced refresh with the token's kid and requestor tenant id; add alert if forced refresh rate spikes.

marie: Ops note: for private deployments (Redwood Private) customers might host IdP behind NAT and we may not reach it; forced refresh must fail gracefully and not block other requests. fallback policy: if forced refresh fails, keep using cached keys for verification but mark tenant degraded and return 503? hmm.

alex: For this Acme case, recommend support steps for CS:
1) Tell Acme to ensure JWKS endpoint returns updated keys immediately after rotation and to include cache-control: no-cache or short max-age until rotation settles.
2) Ask Acme to check time sync on their IdP (NTP) and ensure clock skew < 2min.
3) We can temporarily increase per-tenant JWKS refresh frequency and leeway while they fix rotation.

michael (oncall): i'll patch runtime to implement the forced-refresh-on-signature-fail + 2min leeway. i'll target a hotfix in eng-runtime, and roll out canary to dev first.

marie: add unit tests for:
- kid present in token but not in cache -> fetch+retry
- signature fails with valid kid in remote JWKS -> refresh+retry
- respect forced-refresh rate limit
- iat/exp leeway boundaries

sam: QA scenarios / repro steps for support to attach when escalating:
1) Simulate an IdP rotation: run a local JWKS server that serves old keys, then swap to new keys and set cache-control: max-age=900. Issue tokens with new kid and call our API. Observe 401 until refresh window.
Commands:
```
# start jwks server serving old key
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory jwks_old
# swap to jwks_new dir
mv jwks_new/* jwks_old/
# curl token
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
2) Clock skew repro: create token with iat 90s in future and verify rejection if leeway=30s, acceptance at leeway=120s.

alex: Support reply draft to Acme:
"Thanks for the report — we see your IdP rotated keys at 07:55 UTC which can cause a short window where our cached JWKS doesn't include the new key. We're implementing a mitigation that will cause our verifier to refresh JWKs and retry on signature failures, and we'll increase default clock skew tolerance. In the meantime, can you confirm your IdP is issuing tokens with correct system time (NTP) and consider setting Cache-Control: no-cache on your JWKS endpoint during rotations? We'll also temporarily increase your tenant's JWKS refresh frequency."

michael (oncall): opening internal ticket ENG-5248: "JWKS cache + signature-fail retry + leeway increase" — assigning to eng-runtime.

marie: one more edge: some IdPs rotate keys and reuse old kid values but different alg (RS256 vs ES256) — ensure we validate alg in token header and reject mismatched algs explicitly with a clear error.

kai: also check for alg = "none" attacks; we already reject that but add test.

alex: adding logs we should capture for future triage (structured fields): tenant_id, token_kid, token_alg, verify_err, jwks_cached_version, forced_refresh_bool.

sam: ok will create a templated KB article for CS: "JWT validation failures: kid rotation and JWKS caching" with repro steps, temp mitigations, and the proposed support email text.

marie: anything else?

alex: nope, i'll update the incident thread when patch ships.
